decision.argument_basis: scope evidence not reflected in the mapping
decision.evidence_cited: The employee is described as "Nyx's go-to authority on link-budget modeling for every high-speed interface program company-wide" — domain ownership spanning the entire product roadmap rather than a single product or team, which is the Distinguished MTS indicator, not the Principal MTS indicator of cross-team-but-bounded ownership. This is paired with sustained external recognition (two industry-conference presentations, trade-press coverage, three patents), the specific evidentiary bar Nyx's own document sets for the Fellow honorific. Fellow alone doesn't dictate a level, but here the underlying scope evidence — company-wide, cross-program authority rather than a defined technical area — matches Nyx's top-band anchor, not the level below it.
decision.framework_section: Section 4 (Level anchors — Distinguished MTS row) and Section 6 (Fellow)
